title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 90
paragraphs: While they were preparing to take vengeance, a matter arose from the Lacedaemonians that hindered them. For the Lacedaemonians, having learned of what the Alcmaeonidae had contrived with regard to the Pythian priestess, and of what the Pythian priestess had contrived against themselves and the sons of Peisistratus, were doubly grieved—not only because they had driven into exile men who were their guest-friends, but also because, after having done this, no gratitude was shown to them by the Athenians. Moreover, in addition, they were urged on by oracles that said they would suffer many injuries from the Athenians—oracles they had not been aware of before, but had come to know since Cleomenes had brought them to Sparta. Cleomenes had, in fact, obtained from the Athenian Acropolis those oracles which the sons of Peisistratus had possessed before and had left behind in the temple when they were driven out; and Cleomenes recovered them after they had been left behind.
